ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Diana wants to write whole numbers into each circle in the diagram, so that for all eight small triangles the sum of the three numbers in the corners is always the same. What is the maximum amount of different numbers she can use?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the figure: There are 9 circles in the figure, arranged like a 3×3 square array; there is a center circle in the middle, and 8 outer circles around it form a ring. Adjacent outer circles are connected by line segments, and the center circle is also connected to the surrounding outer circles, thereby forming 8 small triangles. Each small triangle has the center circle and a pair of adjacent outer circles as its three vertices. Then reason: Denote the number in the center circle by c, and denote the 8 outer circles in clockwise order by a1,a2,...,a8. The problem requires that the sums of the numbers on the three corners of the 8 small triangles are all the same, so there is a1+a2+c=a2+a3+c=...=a8+a1+c. Each equation contains the same c; eliminating c gives a1+a2=a2+a3=...=a8+a1. Comparing two adjacent equations, for example a1+a2=a2+a3, gives a1=a3; continuing to compare gives a1=a3=a5=a7, and a2=a4=a6=a8. That is to say, the 8 outer circles can have at most only two different numbers: one kind in the odd positions and one kind in the even positions. The center circle can also use a third different number. Therefore, in total there are at most 3 different numbers. This upper bound can be reached: for example, fill the outer ring alternately with 1 and 2, and fill the center with 3. Each small triangle contains a 1, a 2, and the center 3, so the sums are all the same. Therefore the maximum number of different digits is 3.

raw_record.question_text: Diana wants to write whole numbers into each circle in the diagram, so that for all eight small triangles the sum of the three numbers in the corners is always the same. What is the maximum amount of different numbers she can use?

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram as a center circle surrounded by eight outer circles forming an 8-cycle; each of the eight small triangles consists of the center circle and two neighboring outer circles. Label the outer circles cyclically a1,...,a8 and the center c. From the text, all triangle sums are equal, so a1+a2+c=a2+a3+c=...=a8+a1+c. Cancel c to get that every adjacent outer pair has the same sum: a1+a2=a2+a3=...=a8+a1. Subtract consecutive equations to obtain a1=a3=a5=a7 and a2=a4=a6=a8. Thus the eight outer circles can use at most two different numbers, and the center can use at most one more number, so at most 3 different numbers total. Show attainability by putting one whole number on alternating outer circles, a second whole number on the other alternating outer circles, and a third whole number in the center; then each triangle has one of each outer type plus the center, so all sums match.

先描述图像：图中有9个圆，排成类似3×3方阵；中间有一个中心圆，周围8个外圆围成一圈。相邻外圆之间由线段连接，中心圆也和周围外圆连接，从而形成8个小三角形。每个小三角形都由中心圆和一对相邻的外圆作为三个顶点。

再推理：把中心圆中的数记为c，把8个外圆按顺时针顺序记为a1,a2,...,a8。题目要求8个小三角形三个角上的数之和都相同，所以有
 a1+a2+c=a2+a3+c=...=a8+a1+c。
每个等式中都有同一个c，消去c，得到
 a1+a2=a2+a3=...=a8+a1。
比较相邻两式，例如a1+a2=a2+a3，可得a1=a3；继续比较可得a1=a3=a5=a7，且a2=a4=a6=a8。也就是说，8个外圆最多只能出现两种不同的数：奇数位置一种，偶数位置一种。中心圆还可以使用第三种不同的数。因此总共最多是3种不同的数。

这个上限可以达到：例如把外圈交替填1和2，中心填3。每个小三角形都含有一个1、一个2和中心的3，所以和都相同。因此最大不同数字个数是3。

method.method_draft: View the diagram as two visual classes around the center. Compare adjacent small triangles that share the center and one outer circle. For example, the top-left triangle and the top-right triangle along the top share the top-middle circle and the center, so their equal sums force the two remaining top corner circles to be equal. Repeating this comparison around the diagram forces all four corner-position outer circles to have one common value, and all four side-midpoint outer circles to have another common value. The center circle is not forced to equal either class. Therefore no filling can contain more than three distinct values: corner class, side-midpoint class, and center. This maximum is achieved by assigning three different whole numbers to those three classes.
